evals.name: tautological-assertion
evals.expected_output: A finding that the test never actually expires the token (it sends validToken) yet asserts 401, so the test can't fail for the reason its name claims.
assertions: Output must point out that the test never expires the token (or equivalently, that it doesn't actually verify expired-token handling despite its name)
Output must explain that, as written, the test would still pass even if expired-token handling were broken or removed

evals.name: magic-number-status-code
evals.prompt:
Review this test for best practices:

```python
def test_create_user_returns_created():
    response = client.post('/users', json={'name': 'Ada'})
    assert response.status_code == 201
```
evals.expected_output: A recommendation to replace the bare 201 with a named constant (e.g. HTTPStatus.CREATED or the project's own status constant) rather than a raw numeric literal.
assertions: Output must recommend using a named constant instead of the raw numeric status code 201
Output must not claim the test has no assertions or is otherwise non-functional

evals.name: e2e-should-be-integration
evals.prompt: We have this Playwright E2E test that only calls one backend endpoint and checks the JSON response — it never touches the UI. Should it stay in the E2E suite?
evals.expected_output: A recommendation to move the test down to the integration level, since it only exercises one HTTP endpoint and gets none of the value a browser/full-stack E2E test would provide, while still paying E2E's slower, more expensive cost.
assertions: Output must recommend moving the test to the integration level rather than keeping it in the E2E suite
Output must explain that the test doesn't need a browser or the full stack since it never touches the UI

evals.name: requirement-info-unavailable
evals.expected_output: A statement that whether the test actually matches the requirement can't be verified without the spec/ticket, rather than a guess at what the requirement was, while still reviewing the other aspects of the test (naming, assertion clarity, etc.).
assertions: Output must explicitly state that it cannot verify the test matches the requirement without the spec/ticket, rather than inventing or assuming what the requirement is
Output must still comment on at least one other aspect of the test (e.g. naming, assertion style, coverage) instead of stopping entirely

evals.name: overmocked-unit-test
evals.expected_output: A finding that mocking the database, logger, HTTP client, and config all at once leaves little real behavior under test, plus a note that the assertion only checks that insert was called, not what was inserted or the actual outcome.
assertions: Output must comment on the test mocking every one of its dependencies (database, logger, HTTP client, config)
Output must note that the assertion is weak — it only checks that insert was called, not what data was inserted or the resulting outcome

evals.name: too-broad-should-split
evals.expected_output: A recommendation to split this test into separate tests for signup, login, profile retrieval, and account deletion, since each covers an unrelated behavior that could fail independently, and a single failure here wouldn't say which behavior broke.
assertions: Output must recommend splitting the test into multiple tests, one per distinct behavior (signup, login, profile, deletion)
Output must explain that a failure in this combined test wouldn't clearly indicate which behavior broke

evals.name: propose-deterministic-check
evals.expected_output: A finding that the fixed waits should be replaced by waiting on the actual condition, plus a proposal to enforce it deterministically with a lint rule (playwright/no-wait-for-timeout, or an equivalent restricted-syntax rule) so the recurring pattern is caught automatically rather than re-reviewed by hand.
assertions: Output must flag the fixed waits (waitForTimeout / sleep) and recommend waiting on the actual condition instead

Output must propose a deterministic, automated check — a named lint rule such as playwright/no-wait-for-timeout or an equivalent restricted-syntax rule — to catch this pattern automatically in future, not only fix the three tests shown

evals.name: lint-rule-with-existing-violations
evals.prompt: You flagged the bare `201` in our test as a magic number. We'd like to lint for that, but our test suite has around 400 raw status-code literals already. Should we just turn the rule on?
evals.expected_output: A recommendation to adopt the rule incrementally — freeze the current violations as a baseline, fix as files are touched, and enforce once clean — rather than enabling it outright, because a rule that produces hundreds of unfixed warnings trains the team to ignore the linter.
assertions: Output must recommend adopting the rule incrementally (baseline the existing violations, fix as files are touched, enforce once clean) rather than enabling it outright as a hard failure
Output must explain that a rule producing hundreds of ignored warnings is worse than none, because it erodes trust in the linter's output
